questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.topic: Social Psychology: Diffusion of Responsibility
questions.learningObjective: Identify when responsibility diffuses across a group.
questions.stem: A developer notices a failing build but assumes a teammate will fix it; what concept explains this inaction?

options.text: Responsibility is shared so each person waits for others to act
The developer feels personally responsible and will act immediately
The developer lacks the skill to repair the build
The build failure is too minor to matter
options.misconception: minimizes the problem to avoid action

questions.explanation: Diffusion of responsibility occurs when presence of others reduces felt obligation. The tempting skill-gap idea fails because the barrier is social, not technical.
questions.hint: More people present lowers personal obligation.

questions.stem: A team dashboard shows helping rates drop from 80 percent with one bystander to 30 percent with five; what variable drives this drop?
questions.explanation: As bystander count rises, diffusion of responsibility rises and helping falls. The value five marks the larger group condition where rates bottom out.
questions.hint: Count of bystanders is the moving variable.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.topic: Social Psychology: Pluralistic Ignorance
questions.learningObjective: Explain pluralistic ignorance in a group setting.
questions.stem: Everyone in a standup stays silent about a risky deadline, though each privately doubts it; explain the shared illusion.

answer.exemplar: Each member privately doubts the deadline but assumes others accept it, so no one speaks; the group mistakes silence for agreement, producing pluralistic ignorance.

questions.explanation: Pluralistic ignorance is when individuals privately reject a norm but assume others accept it. Silence is misread as consensus, so the risky deadline stands.

questions.topic: Social Psychology: Conditions Required for Contact to Work

stimulus.body: A company pairs engineers from two departments to solve a shared customer problem, with equal pay grades and manager support. The setup is designed to reduce inter-department bias through structured collaboration.

questions.stem: Which condition is explicitly present in this setup?
questions.explanation: Equal status is present and required. Competition or segregation would undermine the contact hypothesis.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.topic: Social Psychology: Prejudice as an Attribution
questions.stem: A team attributes a rival group's failure to laziness rather than lack of resources, then revises after learning of budget cuts. What two-stage attribution shift occurred?
questions.explanation: Stage one is dispositional blame; stage two is situational revision. Prejudice as attribution favors dispositional explanations for out-groups.
